title: Family Premium Billing, Grace Period and Lockout Terms
content:
A Medicaid Managed Care Membership in a category that bills a family premium is billed, falls due and can be ended for non-payment on the terms below.

## Terms in force

**1. Billing.** A premium is billed only in a category whose premium ladder is not empty, once per coverage month, at the ladder row whose income band contains the household income percent on the membership on the billing date. The premium is per family: it is billed on one membership of the family, the membership of the oldest child, and never on the siblings' memberships.

**2. Due date.** The premium for a coverage month is due on the category's premium due day of the month before that coverage month.

**3. Termination for non-payment.** A membership can be ended for premium non-payment only after the category's premium grace days have fully passed since the due date of the oldest unpaid coverage month. The grace days are counted in calendar days from the day after the due date, and termination is allowed only on a day strictly after the last grace day. The unpaid months and their due dates are read from the membership's premium account as recorded.

**4. Continuous eligibility.** A membership whose continuous eligibility period is running is never ended for premium non-payment; the unpaid premium stays on the premium balance instead.

The category figures these terms read (the premium ladder, the due day, the grace days, the lockout days and the prepayment limit) are the category's own premium terms.

## Retired terms

Each term below is **no longer in force**; it is superseded by the current basis.

- The term that a payment is applied first to the oldest billed coverage month that is not yet paid or waived, and that a payment exceeding all billed months is applied to future months up to the category's prepayment limit, with any remainder returned to the payer.
- The term that, after a termination for premium non-payment, the family may re-enroll in the category within the lockout days only by paying the past-due balance in full.

## Termination for non-payment at a glance

| Facts on the membership | Effect on an ending for non-payment |
|---|---|
| Continuous eligibility period running | No; the unpaid premium stays on the premium balance |
| No continuous eligibility running; the day is on or before the last grace day of the oldest unpaid month | No |
| No continuous eligibility running; the day is strictly after the last grace day of the oldest unpaid month | The grace condition of term 3 is met |

## Hypothetical boundary cases

*Hypothetical dates, for a category whose due day is the 20th and whose grace period is 60 days, with no continuous eligibility running.* The oldest unpaid coverage month is September, so its premium was due on 20 August. The first grace day is 21 August and the last grace day is 19 October.

- On 19 October, the last grace day, the membership cannot yet be ended for non-payment.
- On 20 October, the first day strictly after the last grace day, the grace condition of term 3 is met.

## Hypothetical billing case

*Hypothetical family.* Two children of one family both hold memberships in a premium-billing category. The premium is billed once per coverage month on the older child's membership and not on the younger child's.
